summary: Single deployable monolith: React Native (Expo) (Android) on Python 3.13 + Django 5.2 LTS with Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server 17 — Central India (Pune), hosted on Azure App Service (Linux, Basic B1) — Central India (Pune). Estimated $29-86/month.

frontend.justification: Mobile: React Native (Expo) — Team already writes javascript for the mobile app; mature on-device storage and background sync; good fast delivery (priority 4/5); good low running cost (priority 5/5).

alternatives.why_not: Team lists javascript, python but this needs kotlin/java (team.languages). React Native (Expo) is stronger on: good fast delivery (priority 4/5) (priorities.time_to_market). Overall 6.8 points behind. Known limit of Kotlin + Jetpack Compose: android only; iOS needs a second codebase.

Heavier runtime on low-end phones (project.description); weaker performance (priority 3/5) (priorities.performance). Overall 7.4 points behind. Known limit of Ionic Capacitor: webView performance on low-end devices.

tradeoffs: JS runtime overhead on very low-end phones

what_would_change.new_choice: No single-field edit among the probed priorities, requirements, numbers and constraints changes this choice.

backend.justification: Team already writes python for the API; good low running cost (priority 5/5); good maintainability (priority 4/5).

alternatives.why_not: Python 3.13 + Django 5.2 LTS is stronger on: good fast delivery (priority 4/5) (priorities.time_to_market); good security (priority 3/5) (priorities.security). Overall 1.0 points behind. Known limit of Node.js 24 LTS + NestJS: more boilerplate than Express.

Python 3.13 + Django 5.2 LTS is stronger on: good maintainability (priority 4/5) (priorities.maintainability); good fast delivery (priority 4/5) (priorities.time_to_market). Overall 4.8 points behind. Known limit of Python 3.13 + FastAPI: bring-your-own admin/auth pieces.

database.choice: Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server 17 — Central India (Pune)
database.justification: Handles write-heavy load; good low running cost (priority 5/5); good maintainability (priority 4/5).

alternatives.choice: Azure Database for MySQL – Flexible Server 8.4
alternatives.why_not: Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server 17 is stronger on: good maintainability (priority 4/5) (priorities.maintainability); good security (priority 3/5) (priorities.security). Overall 5.6 points behind. Known limit of Azure Database for MySQL – Flexible Server 8.4: 8.0 moved to Sustaining Support (Apr 2026); no row-level security.

Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server 17 is stronger on: good low running cost (priority 5/5) (priorities.cost). Overall 8.0 points behind. Known limit of Azure SQL Database: licence cost outside Azure SQL; Windows-centric tooling.

tradeoffs: Vertical write scaling; sharding needs extensions

what_would_change.new_choice: No single-field edit among the probed priorities, requirements, numbers and constraints changes this choice (the managed provider still follows the hosting choice).

hosting.choice: Azure App Service (Linux, Basic B1) — Central India (Pune)
hosting.justification: Satisfies the hard constraints (managed_cloud (no servers to patch), data_residency india -> Central India (Pune)). Fully managed runtime (patching, TLS, scaling handled) for a team without a DevOps person; good maintainability (priority 4/5); good fast delivery (priority 4/5).

alternatives.why_not: Azure App Service (Linux, Basic B1) is stronger on: good maintainability (priority 4/5) (priorities.maintainability); good fast delivery (priority 4/5) (priorities.time_to_market). Overall 0.8 points behind. Known limit of Google Cloud Run: cold starts unless min instances are paid for.

Operations burden 2/5 with no dedicated DevOps person (team.has_devops). Azure App Service (Linux, Basic B1) is stronger on: good maintainability (priority 4/5) (priorities.maintainability). Overall 9.9 points behind. Known limit of Azure Container Apps: more moving parts than App Service for a single web app.
Excluded: no INDIA region for application data (infrastructure.data_residency).

tradeoffs: Less control than containers for unusual runtimes

supporting.justification: phone_otp for Indian users: an Indian SMS provider with DLT-registered templates is the cheapest reliable OTP route (about Rs 0.20 per SMS); the backend stores users and refresh tokens in the in-region database.

alternatives.why_not: stores identity data in Google's global auth service, conflicting with India residency
about $0.05 per verification plus SMS, far above Indian SMS rates

tradeoffs: DLT registration of sender ID/template before launch
OTP needs network at login; sessions must stay valid offline

supporting.justification: Uploads (GPS-tagged photos) go straight from clients to object storage via signed URLs. Private bucket, server-generated signed URLs, encryption with managed keys.

alternatives.why_not: bloats backups and costs more per GB
zero egress fees, but a second vendor outside AZURE

supporting.choice: Azure Service Bus in Central India (Pune)
supporting.justification: Background work: photo post-processing (thumbnails, EXIF/GPS extraction) after bursts of offline syncs.

alternatives.why_not: slow responses and lost work when a call fails

supporting.justification: Automated tests and deploys on every push to Azure App Service (Linux, Basic B1); free minutes cover a team of 2.

alternatives.why_not: equivalent; GitHub chosen for its marketplace of deploy actions

tradeoffs: Secrets must be stored as encrypted environment secrets

supporting.choice: Azure Monitor + Application Insights in Central India (Pune)
supporting.justification: Logs and metrics stay with the host provider in Central India (Pune); alerts on error rate and latency.

alternatives.why_not: stores data only in the US or EU

tradeoffs: Log retention costs grow with traffic

supporting.choice: Offline-first sync: expo-sqlite + background task, outbox + idempotent sync API
supporting.justification: Must work without connectivity: writes go to an on-device database first; an outbox queue retries uploads when signal returns; each record carries a client-generated UUID so retries are idempotent; server applies last-writer-wins per field with an edit log; photos are compressed on-device and uploaded with resumable chunks; sync batches are small and compressed for 2G/3G.

alternatives.why_not: convenient but ties data to Google's global service and its pricing

tradeoffs: Conflict resolution rules must be agreed with field teams
Device storage limits on low-end phones

assumptions: Hosting Azure App Service (Linux, Basic B1): $13-30/month at the 'tiny' tier.
Database Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server 17: $13-30/month.
queue: Azure Service Bus in Central India (Pune) $0-1/month.
observability: Azure Monitor + Application Insights in Central India (Pune) $0-5/month.
Stored data ~100 GB after 12 months at ~$0.02-0.035/GB-month (year-end volume used as an upper bound, not an average).
Phone OTP: 2,000 users x 0.3-1.0 OTP logins/month at India SMS ~Rs 0.20-0.25 + GST per SMS = $1-9/month (long-lived sessions keep OTPs rare).
Excluded: taxes, domain names, paid support plans and data-egress spikes. Order-of-magnitude band, not a quote.

warnings.message: Phone OTP needs signal at first login; sessions are long-lived refresh tokens so the app keeps working offline afterwards.

DPDP Act 2023: collect consent with a clear notice, support access/correction/erasure requests, keep breach-notification runbooks (72 h to the Board under the 2025 Rules) and delete data when the purpose ends. Hosting in India simplifies transfers; legal review still required.

assumptions: requirements.p95_latency_ms absent or null: no explicit latency target; typical web latency assumed.
Knowledge base as of 2026-11-10; lifecycle and pricing judgements use that date, not the run date.
Scale tier 'tiny' from 2,000 users and ~200 peak concurrent users (people, not requests per second; used only for sizing and cost).
